config.title: Write a balanced parentheses checker

intro.title: Write a balanced parentheses checker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that checks if a string of parentheses is balanced. A balanced string means every opening parenthesis '(' has a corresponding closing parenthesis ')' in the correct order. You will learn to use a stack data structure to track parentheses as you iterate through the string. This exercise will help you practice fundamental JavaScript concepts like loops, conditionals, and array methods. By the end, you'll have a working checker that returns true for balanced strings and false for unbalanced ones.
intro.usecase: Balanced parentheses checking is essential in code editors and IDEs like VS Code, which validate syntax in real-time by ensuring every opening bracket has a matching closing one. This pattern also powers form validation in web applications, such as checking mathematical expressions in calculator inputs or JSON/XML structures in configuration panels. Developers implement these checkers to prevent runtime errors in templating engines, build tools that parse configuration files, and even in UI component libraries that dynamically render nested components.

objectives: Implement a function that accepts a string of parentheses as input
Initialize a stack data structure to track opening parentheses
Manipulate the stack by pushing opening parentheses and popping on matches
Control the iteration through each character in the input string
Construct a validation condition that returns true for balanced parentheses
Configure the function to return false for any unbalanced or mismatched parentheses
Integrate the checker function into a simple test to verify correctness

steps.title: Create the main function and import any needed utilities
steps.instruction: Create a function named isBalanced that takes a string parameter. No imports are needed for this basic implementation.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name 'isBalanced' that accepts one parameter representing the input string.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function named isBalanced that takes a string parameter, ready for implementing the parentheses checking logic.
successCriteria: The function isBalanced is defined with one string parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named exactly 'isBalanced' and accepts one string parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'isBalanced' and included a parameter for the input string.

steps.title: Initialize a stack data structure
steps.instruction: Inside your isBalanced function, create an empty array that will serve as a stack to track opening parentheses.
steps.hint: You can declare a variable and assign it an empty array using let stack = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now contain an empty array variable that will be used as a stack.
successCriteria: The isBalanced function contains a variable declaration for an empty array named 'stack'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a variable named 'stack' and assigned it an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't contain an empty array variable named 'stack'. Try declaring 'let stack = [];' inside the function.

steps.title: Define a mapping of closing to opening parentheses
steps.instruction: Inside the isBalanced function, create a constant object named 'pairs' that maps each closing parenthesis character (')', ']', '}') to its corresponding opening character ('(', '[', '{').
steps.hint: You can define an object using curly braces with key-value pairs. For example, ')': '(' would be one mapping.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a 'pairs' object that can be used to check matching parentheses later.
successCriteria: A constant named 'pairs' is defined as an object with three key-value pairs: ')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your pairs object includes all three closing-to-opening mappings: ')', ']', and '}'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The pairs mapping object is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a constant named 'pairs' with closing parentheses as keys and their matching opening parentheses as values.

steps.title: Loop through each character of the input string
steps.instruction: Inside your isBalanced function, add a for loop that iterates through each character of the input string 'str'.
steps.hint: You can use a standard for loop with a counter variable (like i) that goes from 0 to the length of the string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a loop structure ready to process each character in the next steps.
successCriteria: A for loop is added inside the function that iterates through each character of the input string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your loop correctly iterates through each character of the string 'str'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a for loop inside the function that iterates through the string.

steps.title: Check if the character is an opening parenthesis
steps.instruction: Inside your for loop, add an if statement to check if the current character is an opening parenthesis: '(' or '[' or '{'. If it is, push that character onto the stack.
steps.hint: You can use the logical OR operator (||) to check multiple conditions in one if statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function will now identify opening parentheses and push them onto the stack for later matching.
successCriteria: The for loop contains an if statement that checks if the current character is '(', '[', or '{' and pushes it onto the stack when true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your if statement checks for all three opening parentheses types: '(', '[', and '{'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the for loop, add an if statement that checks if the character is an opening parenthesis and pushes it to the stack.

steps.title: Handle closing parentheses
steps.instruction: Inside your for loop, add an else if condition to check if the current character is a closing parenthesis (')', ']', or '}').
steps.hint: You can check if the character exists as a key in your pairs object to determine if it's a closing parenthesis.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function should now include logic to identify closing parentheses within the loop.
successCriteria: The else if condition checks if the current character is a closing parenthesis using the pairs object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking if the character is a closing parenthesis by looking it up in the pairs object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to add an else if condition that checks if the current character is a closing parenthesis (')', ']', or '}').

steps.title: Check for matching opening parenthesis on the stack
steps.instruction: Inside the closing parenthesis condition, check if the stack is empty OR if the last item popped from the stack doesn't match the expected opening parenthesis from your mapping object. If either is true, return false.
steps.hint: Use the stack array's pop() method to remove and get the last element. Compare it with pairs[char] using !==.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now detect mismatched parentheses early and return false when a closing parenthesis doesn't match the most recent opening one on the stack.
successCriteria: The closing parenthesis condition includes a check for stack emptiness and a comparison between the popped stack item and pairs[char], returning false if either condition is true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check both conditions: if the stack is empty OR if the popped item doesn't match the expected opening parenthesis. Both should cause the function to return false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation for closing parentheses is missing or incorrect. Inside the closing condition, you need to pop from the stack and compare it with pairs[char], returning false if they don't match or if the stack is empty.

steps.title: Return true if the stack is empty after the loop
steps.instruction: After the for loop ends, add a return statement that returns true only if the stack is empty. Otherwise, return false.
steps.hint: You can check if the stack is empty by verifying its length is 0. Use a simple return statement with a condition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now have a return statement after the loop that returns true when the stack is empty (all parentheses matched) and false otherwise.
successCriteria: The isBalanced function returns true if the stack is empty after processing all characters, and false if the stack is not empty.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement checks if the stack is empty (stack.length === 0) and returns the appropriate boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement is missing or incorrect. After the loop, you need to return true only if the stack is empty, otherwise return false.

steps.title: Create a test input variable
steps.instruction: Outside the isBalanced function, create a variable named testString and assign it a string containing parentheses to test your function (e.g., '({[]})').
steps.hint: Declare a variable with const or let and assign it a string value that includes parentheses, brackets, or braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a test variable
const testInput = 'hello world';
steps.expectedOutcome: A variable named testString is declared outside the function with a string value containing parentheses.
successCriteria: The testString variable is declared with a string value that includes parentheses, brackets, or braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a variable, but make sure it's named testString and contains parentheses in its value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a variable named testString with a string value containing parentheses. Try declaring a variable like const testString = '({[]})';

steps.title: Call the function and log the result
steps.instruction: Call the isBalanced function with your test string and log the result to the console.
steps.hint: Use console.log() with the function call inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function is called and its result is printed to the console.
successCriteria: isBalanced is called with the test string and the result is logged using console.log.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling isBalanced with your test string and logging the result with console.log.
steps.feedbackWrong: call the isBalanced function with your test string and log the result using console.log().
